'''Leah Edelstein-Keshet''' ({{Langx|he|לאה אדלשטיין-קשת}}) is an Israeli-Canadian [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|mathematical biologist]].

Edelstein-Keshet is known for her contributions to the field of mathematical biology and biophysics.[https://www.smb.org/leah-edelstein-keshet-prize/] Her research spans many topics including sub-cellular biology, ecology, and biomedical research,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://pwias.ubc.ca/profile/leah-edelstein-keshet|title=Leah Edelstein-Keshet|date=2016-07-25|work=Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies|access-date=2018-09-22}}</ref> with particular focus on [[cell motility]] and the [[cytoskeleton]], modeling of  physiology and diseases, such as autoimmune diabetes, and swarming and aggregation behavior in social organisms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/nature-or-nurture-my-mathematical-biology-upbringing|title=Nature or Nurture? My Mathematical Biology Upbringing|last=Edelstein-Keshet|first=Leah|date=February 20, 2004}}</ref>

She is a full-time professor at the [[University of British Columbia]] in Vancouver, Canada.

== Early life and education ==
Edelstein-Keshet was born in Israel, and moved to Canada with her parents when she was 12.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.biophysics.org/Portals/1/PDFs/Career%20Center/Profiles/L_Edelstein-Keshet_profile.pdf|title=Biophysicist in Profile|date=April 2013|website=Biophysical Society Newsletter|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224105653/http://www.biophysics.org/Portals/1/PDFs/Career%20Center/Profiles/L_Edelstein-Keshet_profile.pdf|archive-date=2013-12-24|url-status=dead}}</ref> She earned her Bachelor of Science and Master of Science in Mathematics from [[Dalhousie University]] and received in 1982 her doctorate in Applied Mathematics from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in Israel, where she was supervised by [[Lee Segel]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://pwias.ubc.ca/profile/leah-edelstein-keshet|title=Leah Edelstein-Keshet|date=2016-07-25|work=Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies|access-date=2018-09-22}}</ref>

== Career ==
Edelstein-Keshet held teaching positions at [[Brown University]] and [[Duke University]] before joining the [[University of British Columbia]] as an associate professor in 1989, where she is now Associate Head (Faculty Affairs).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.ubc.ca/People/people.shtml|title=Department Directory|website=www.math.ubc.ca|access-date=2019-10-08|archive-date=2021-04-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417135644/https://www.math.ubc.ca/People/people.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has authored three books, including ''Mathematical Models in Biology'' in the SIAM Series and ''Classics in Applied Mathematics''. In 1995 she became the first female president of the [[Society for Mathematical Biology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.ubc.ca/~keshet/keshet.html|title=Leah Edelstein-Keshet|website=www.math.ubc.ca}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2003 she was awarded the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ca/Prizes/citations/kn2003.pdf|title=Krieger–Nelson Prize Citation|author=|year=2003|work=Le Prix Krieger-Nelson 2003 Krieger-Nelson Prize|publisher=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=6 February 2011}}</ref> She became a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2014 "for contributions to the mathematics and modeling of the cell, the immune system, and biological swarms, as well as to applied mathematics education".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2014|title=SIAM Fellows|website=fellows.siam.org}}</ref> She was also awarded a Faculty of Science Award for Leadership from the [[University of British Columbia]]. She is the 2022 SIAM John von Neumann Prize Lecturer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leah Edelstein-Keshet is the 2022 SIAM John von Neumann Prize Lecturer |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/leah-edelstein-keshet-is-the-2022-siam-john-von-neumann-prize-lecturer |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=SIAM News |date=21 December 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref>
